source: Locally authored software facts and relevance judgments. Pipeline verification only, not a research-quality corpus.

documents.text: BM25 ranks documents using term frequency saturation and inverse document frequency. It normalizes for document length.
Dense retrieval encodes queries and passages into vectors. Semantic similarity can match related meanings with no shared words.
Reciprocal rank fusion combines ordered retrieval lists without requiring calibrated similarity scores.
A cross encoder jointly processes a query and passage. Reranking improves ordering but adds inference latency.
SQLite write ahead logging permits concurrent readers while a single writer updates the database.
Docker network isolation prevents a container from connecting to external services. Memory and CPU limits constrain resources.
Recall at k is the fraction of relevant documents found in the first k search results.
Precision at k is the fraction of the first k search results that are relevant.
NDCG discounts relevant documents by rank and normalizes discounted gain against the ideal ordering.
Mean reciprocal rank averages the inverse position of the first relevant result for each query.
Caching query embeddings avoids repeated encoder computation for repeated queries. Cache invalidation tracks model versions.
Chunk overlap preserves context across boundaries but increases index size and repeated text in retrieved passages.
Paired bootstrap resamples query-level paired differences to estimate uncertainty in benchmark improvement.
Training on evaluation labels causes data leakage. Held-out queries must be separate from tuning data.
Quantization reduces model weight precision to decrease memory use. Four-bit weights require less VRAM than full precision.
Approximate nearest neighbor indexes trade exact vector search recall for reduced query latency.
Stop words occur frequently in text and often carry little discriminative retrieval information.
Stemming maps related inflected words to a shared root, allowing lexical matches across word forms.
Hybrid retrieval combines lexical matching with semantic vector search to cover different query types.
Evidence-based faithfulness evaluates whether generated answers are supported by retrieved passages.
